statement.p: A differentiable function f(x,y) has the property that f(5,4)=6 and f_x(5,4)=-3 and f_y(5,4)=3. Find the equation of the tangent plane at the point on the surface z=f(x,y) where x=5, y=4.

static.solution: (5,4,6) lies on the surface. The surface is the level surface of the function F(x,y,z) = f(x,y) - z = 0 . The normal to the surface at the point (5,4,6) is \nabla F(5,4,6) = f_x(5,4)\vec i + f_y(5,4)\vec j - \vec k= -3 \vec i + 3 \vec j - \vec k. Thus the equation of the tangent plane is -3 x + 3 y - z = -3 (5) + 3 (4) - 6 or z = 6+\left(-3\right)\mathopen{}\left(x-5\right)+3\mathopen{}\left(y-4\right).
